title: Apple is running macOS on an iPad, but you won't be able to
summary: Apple has macOS running on iPads internally, but despite the existence of the cross-platform experiment, it's far from becoming a reality for users anytime soon. macOS on an iPad would make the tablet be even more like a notebook. The idea of having an iPad that runs on macOS has been a dream scenario for some Mac users, but it has never officially become a reality. However, while the public isn't getting access to such a device in the foreseeable future, Apple is already experimenting with it. Answering a listener's question on his "Power On" podcast for Bloomberg , Mark Gurman says that Apple has iPads running macOS internally. Apple apparently, and perhaps obviously, has been running it for a while already. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

title: Image Playground is finally decent, and it's about time
summary: Apple's Image Playground is finally worth using, with better image generation and natural-language photo editing turning the once-limited Apple Intelligence feature into a practical creative tool. Image Playground, generated with same The improvements go beyond photorealistic images. Users can now edit existing photographs by describing what they want to change, while new controls make it easier to refine generated artwork. In my testing, I used one of Image Playground's suggested prompts to add a lake to an existing image. The app followed my instructions and produced a result I liked, demonstrating how useful its editing tools can be for straightforward adjustments. Image quality has also improved considerably since the original release, and the app has generally handled my prompts well. Apple still needs to offer more aspect ratios and creative controls, but Image Playground has become a decent alternative to ChatGPT for everyday photo editing. title: What to watch for after the new 1Password data breach
summary: 1Password is warning customers to watch for phishing scams after an attacker used an employee's GitHub account to steal customer records. 1Password breach exposes customer account data An attacker breached 1Password's backend systems and copied customer names, email addresses, and other account data. The company said customer vaults, their contents, and the keys protecting them were unaffected. According to 1Password, an investigation began on November 19, 2026, after 1Password detected signs that someone had accessed an employee's corporate GitHub account.
